source.title: Door input shows with no Room and sits badly at the window edge
source.body:
User report, from a screenshot: the input for the Door is badly placed, undesigned, and should appear only when a Room exists (a Workstream after #369).

Seen in the screenshot: with "no Room yet / + start a Room" in the centre, the Door input still shows at the bottom edge of the window. It touches the edge with no margin, wears a bare blue focus border, and carries an error line above it: "select a Room to talk to its Door". The input has focus before the user asked for it.

Expected:
- With no Room, no input and no error. The empty state offers the one entry point (#369).
- With a Room, the input sits inside the Room view with margin and a designed surface, Tokens only, and a clear send action.
- No input error for a state the UI can prevent.

Related: #355, #369, #389 (the Door receives the user's asks), #400.
Report only; no code change performed.

goals.statement: With no Room in the selection (an empty Project, no row selected, or a selected row with no Room among itself and its ancestors), the centre shows no Thread input, no feed, no send action and no input error; U143's `no Room yet` / `start a Room` is the only entry point in the centre.
goals.observer: U26 harness `?seed=empty-project` at 1280x800 and 700x800 in agent-browser: `document.querySelector('[data-thread-input]') === null`, no `.thread-failure` text, and the only centre button is `start a Room`; plus `u145_` Vitest for the root-Terminal-only case.

goals.statement: With a Room selected (or a row inside one), the Thread's composer sits inside the centre, inset from its bottom, left and right edges by at least `--space-3`, on its own Token surface (`--sunken`, one 1 px `--hairline` border, `--radius-control`), with the one focus ring on the composer and no second outline on the bare input, and `window.__checks()` D1, D2, D6, D7 and D8 do not regress against main.
goals.observer: U26 harness `?seed=door-stopped` with its Room selected, at 1280x800 and 700x800: composer vs centre `getBoundingClientRect` insets, computed background/border/radius, focus look after Tab, and `window.__checks()` compared to main; captures in `artifacts/ux/U145/`.

goals.statement: A Room's composer has a clear send action: a native `send` button at its trailing end that sends exactly what Enter sends, and is disabled (`aria-disabled`, `--grey`, calls nothing) while there is no text, Quote or Attachment.
goals.observer: `u145_` Vitest against the fake App seam: pointer, Enter and Space on `send` each make one `message.send` identical to Enter's; disabled state makes none; harness capture shows the button.

goals.statement: No input error is shown for a state the UI can prevent: the string `select a Room to talk to its Door` is produced by no code path, and the failure line only carries real failures such as a rejected `message.send` (U80).
goals.observer: `git grep 'select a Room to talk to its Door' -- apps/` returns nothing on main; `u145_` Vitest asserts a rejected `message.send` shows its message and nothing else appears there.

goals.statement: The Thread's input never takes focus before the user asks: opening a Project, selecting a row by pointer, `start a Room` and starting its Door leave focus outside the Thread; only a pointer, Tab or `⌥0` focuses it.
goals.observer: `u145_` Vitest reading `document.activeElement` after each step; harness `document.activeElement` on load of `?seed=door-stopped` and `?seed=empty-project`.

deliveries.title: U145 (specify): the Thread's input shows only where it has a Door
deliveries.body:
## Outcome
A scenario on main, U145 in `scenarios/ui-first-journey.md`, decides when and how the Thread's input shows: no Thread without a Room, an inset composer on Token surfaces with a `send` button, no input error for a state the UI prevents, and no focus taken unasked. Its implementation Issue becomes eligible once this merges.

Found by #440. Today `apps/desktop/src/App.tsx` mounts `<Thread>` under every centre, including U143's `no Room yet`. `apps/desktop/src/thread/Thread.tsx` sets `select a Room to talk to its Door` when `doorId()` is null. `thread/styles.css` gives the composer no inset and no surface (a transparent, borderless input under the global `:focus-visible` ring). No scenario in U105–U110 (`ui-attention.md`) or U143 decides when the input shows.

## Scope
`scenarios/ui-first-journey.md` only: add U145, update the `Ids:` line to `U143, U144, U145`, and correct the stale "Capability against UI" paragraph, which says no desktop UI calls `message.send` even though #411 landed the Thread. No code, no contract, no App seam command, no Token. `GLOSSARY.md` stays as is: the scenario uses Room, Door, Thread, Quote, Attachment and Token as defined.

Proposed U145 text: the rule proposal for `scenarios/ui-first-journey.md` in plan run https://github.com/saadshahd/roundup/actions/runs/37963935192. The spec Builder may tighten the wording and keep every clause.

## Acceptance
- `scenarios/ui-first-journey.md` on main holds U145 with the clauses No Room, A Room, Send, Focus and Errors, a `u145_` test list and a browser observer. Each clause has a pass condition a test or the harness reads: DOM presence, `getBoundingClientRect` insets, computed Token values, `document.activeElement`, and `message.send` call counts.
- U145 names what it narrows (U105–U110, U143) and states that it changes no contract, App seam command or Token.
- The PR closes this Issue. The implementation Issue (Key U145) is filed blocked by this one.

Observer: independent review of the scenario diff against #440's Expected list. Each of #440's three Expected bullets maps to a U145 clause with a pass condition.

## Preserve
- U143's wording and its `start a Room` path, plus U107's `⌥0` (it ends a Takeover; with no Thread it focuses nothing).
- U105 dim, U106 fold, U109 Attachment and U110 Quote behaviour inside a Room's Thread.
- Direct Agent access (P1).
- The rename of Room to Workstream (#369) is a separate change. U145 must not anticipate it.
- #355 and #400 (window and button design) stay their own feedback. U145 decides only the Thread's composer.

## Queue
Scenarios: U145
Specification: [scenarios/ui-first-journey.md](https://github.com/saadshahd/roundup/blob/main/scenarios/ui-first-journey.md)
Key: U145-spec
Priority: 20
Mode: specify
Provider: any

rules.content:
# UI: the first Room (U143)

Module: `apps/desktop` (the webview). Ids: U143, U144, U145. Found by walking the first journey in the U26 harness: an open Project with no row says only `select an agent or a terminal` and offers no first action in the centre; a Room whose Door is not running shows a bare `start Door`, so a Door that never launched, one that stopped, one that is starting and one that failed to start look the same.

**U143 the first Room says where it stands.** Narrows U38 and U9; changes no contract, App seam command or token. Given an open Project, then:

- **Empty.** Only when `rail.tree` has no row, the centre replaces U38's `select an agent or a terminal` with a light `no Room yet` and one button, `start a Room`. The button runs the same path as the Rail's `+ room` (U9): one `rail.createRoom {name: "room", parent: null}`, then select the returned Room once `rail.tree` has its row, then one `rail.startDoor {id}`. It is a native button, so Tab reaches it and Enter or Space activates it. While creation is pending the line reads `creating Room…`, the button is disabled, and a second activation of it or of `+ room` calls nothing (U9). A failed creation shows its message as an alert, selects nothing, starts no Door, and leaves the button ready to try again. A failed Door launch afterwards retries that same Room through U9's `retry Door`; it never creates another. With any row present and none selected, U38's text and no button show. The Rail's `no agents yet` / `⌘N starts one`, `+ agent` and `+ terminal` are unchanged, so direct Agent access stays.
- **Door states.** When the selected row is a Room whose Door has no running program, the centre shows one light state line above U9's `start Door` / `retry Door`, in a fixed block that does not resize the pane. The line is one of:
  - `starting Door…` while a `rail.startDoor` call is pending; the button is disabled, so a repeat activation calls nothing (U9);
  - `Door did not start` after a failed start (U9), beside the `✕ <message>` line and `retry Door`;
  - `Door not started` when the Room has no Attempt (A20) and no Terminal;
  - `Door stopped` when it has an Attempt and no running program, followed by `, exited <code>` or `, exited by signal` when the ending is known (U7's wording). `stopped` means launched before and not running now, however it ended, so a Room whose first launch failed reads `stopped` after a reload.
- **Running.** A Room with a running Door shows its Terminal and no state line. The words never mention a Thread or coordination: today the Thread is the Door's Terminal (`GLOSSARY.md`).
- **Direct access.** With a stopped Door selected, `+ agent` and `+ terminal` still spawn inside that Room (U9).

Tests are named `u143_…`: `apps/desktop/src/rail/doorState.test.ts` (the four states and their words) and `apps/desktop/src/terminal/u143_door_states.test.tsx` (the rendered App against the fake App seam, including keyboard focus, pending and repeat activation). Observer: the U26 harness at 1280 by 800 and 700 by 800, `?seed=agents-10` with its rows removed through `rail.remove` (an already open, empty Project), then `start a Room`, a failed start (`__fake.failNext`), the Rail menu's `stop`, and a `terminal.exited` with a code. `window.__checks()` must not regress against `main`: the full before/after readings and screenshots are in `artifacts/ux/U143/`. D1, D2, D7, D8 and D10 already fail on both observed screens; D6 additionally fails with a stopped Door. D3, D4, D5 and D9 stay passing. This scenario weakens no Check. Percy also captures the `empty-project` and `door-stopped` seeds, with the stopped Room selected before rendering. The native folder chooser is not covered by this browser observer. The fake answers at once, so `creating Room…` and `starting Door…` are observed in Vitest with a held promise, not in a screenshot.

Capability against UI. The Thread's input, Messages to a Door and Routes have contracts (`message.send`, `message.list`, `route.set`, `takeover.begin`, `decision.list`; `contracts/generated/methods.ts`) but no desktop UI calls them; U105 to U110 (`ui-attention.md`) already own that UI and wait on the Door scenarios. Until it lands, a Room's conversation is its Door's Terminal and this slice claims nothing more. A summary of settled work (P1's observer) has no method; Todos have the Project-wide `todo.*` methods and a Shelf UI; their contract has no Room field. Room-scoped Todos need a contract decision before a Builder can implement them.

**U144 the harness serves the App on a real Daemon.** Found by the J2 audit: the Enter, Request and Review stages are observed only on the fake Daemon, because the webview reaches a Daemon only through Tauri commands (`apps/desktop/src/app/seam.ts`). Given a running `rupd` for a temporary Project and `just harness-real <project-path> <port>`, then `http://localhost:<port>/harness.html?daemon=1` mounts the same App with an AppSeam whose `rpc` and `subscribe` are served by the dev server over that `rupd`'s socket (`rpc::socket_path`) and whose `project`, `openProject` and `daemonProof` answer from the path given at start. Choosers return `null`, the Dock badge does nothing, and `daemon-exited` fires when the socket closes. Nothing else of the App differs, and `?seed=` behaves as today. It is a development tool: `vite build` leaves it out of `dist`, and it listens on loopback only.

Observer: `u144_` tests in `apps/desktop/src/testing/` start the real `rupd` with the fake `claude` of `crates/rup/tests/e2e/fake_claude.py`, mount the App through the served seam, create a Room and start its Door by pointer, and assert the Terminal and Rail row come from the Daemon, not from a seed. They then close the socket and assert the U25 failure state, and call a method the Daemon rejects and assert its message is shown. `agent-browser` captures at 1280 by 800 and 700 by 800 go to `artifacts/ux/U144/`. This is a webview proof against the real Daemon; the native chooser, WKWebView and a real `claude` remain the user's macOS and F7's observers. It adds no RPC method, App seam command or token.

**U145 the Thread's input shows only where it has a Door.** Found by the user's report #440: with `no Room yet` in the centre, the Thread's input still sat at the window's bottom edge with no margin, an outline on a borderless field, and the line `select a Room to talk to its Door` above it. Rule: a control shows only while the thing it acts on exists, and the UI never offers an action and then answers it with an error for a state the UI itself could have prevented. Narrows U105 to U110 and U143; changes no contract, App seam command or Token. Given an open Project, then:

- **No Room.** While the selection resolves to no Room (no row at all, no row selected, or a selected row with no Room among itself and its ancestors), the centre has no Thread: no `[data-thread-input]`, no feed, no failure line and no send action. U143's `no Room yet` and `start a Room` are the only action in the centre. `⌥0` (U107) still ends a Takeover and focuses nothing. No code path produces `select a Room to talk to its Door`.
- **A Room.** While the selected row is a Room or lies under one, whatever its Door's state (U143), the Thread shows inside the centre below the pane. Its composer is inset from the centre's bottom, left and right edges by `--space-3` or more, rests on its own surface (`--sunken`, one 1 px `--hairline` border, `--radius-control`), and uses only Tokens. When the input has keyboard focus the composer shows the one focus ring (`docs/design-system.md`, "Click targets") and the input draws no second outline.
- **Send.** A native `send` button sits at the composer's trailing end. Activating it, by pointer, Enter or Space, sends exactly what Enter in the input sends (U105, U109, U110). While the input is empty and no Quote or Attachment waits it is disabled (`aria-disabled`, `--grey`) and calls nothing. It meets D6 and D7.
- **Focus.** Opening a Project, selecting a row by pointer, creating a Room and starting its Door move no focus into the Thread. The input takes focus only from a pointer, Tab or `⌥0`.
- **Errors.** A failed `message.send` still shows its message on U80's one line; no other line shows there.

Tests are named `u145_…` in `apps/desktop/src/thread/` against the fake App seam: an empty Project, a Project whose only row is a root Terminal, a selected Room, an Agent inside a Room, the send button by pointer and keyboard, its disabled state, the focus after `start a Room`, and a rejected `message.send`. Observer: the U26 harness at 1280 by 800 and 700 by 800 with `?seed=empty-project` (no Thread in the DOM) and `?seed=door-stopped` with its Room selected (the composer's insets read from `getBoundingClientRect`, its computed surface, and `document.activeElement` before any input). `window.__checks()` must not regress against `main` for D1, D2, D6, D7 and D8; captures go to `artifacts/ux/U145/`. Room becoming Workstream (#369) renames this scenario's words with every other one and does not change it.
rules.cases:
Rule: a control shows only while the thing it acts on exists, and the UI never offers an action and then answers it with an error for a state the UI itself could have prevented.
Cases (from context):
- #440: Thread input with no Room. Wrong: input shown, then `select a Room to talk to its Door` on submit. Right: no input and no error; `start a Room` is the entry point.
- A root-level Terminal is selected and no Room is above it (`doorId()` is null in Thread.tsx). Wrong: same error. Right: no Thread.
- U143 `start a Room` while creation is pending. Right (already): disabled, calls nothing, no error.
- U143 `start Door` while starting. Right (already): disabled.
- A rejected `message.send` (Daemon refuses). The UI cannot prevent this, so it shows the error on U80's line (allowed).
- U109: a non-image file is dropped. The UI cannot know the file kind before the drop, so a refusal line is allowed.
Probes (the answer the rule forces):
1. `send` with an empty input and no Quote or Attachment: disabled, no call, no error.
2. The selected Room is removed while the input has text: the Thread unmounts; no error.
3. A stopped Door's Room is selected: the Thread shows (the Room exists); sending is the Daemon's call to refuse.
4. `⌥0` with no Room: ends any Takeover, focuses nothing, no error.
5. A Drawer action whose target row was removed: the action hides, with no `not found` line.
6. `+ agent` inside a Room whose creation is pending: hidden or disabled until the Room exists.
7. Quote from a Terminal selection with no Room: no input exists, so no Quote is made.
8. Daemon exited (U25): inputs that need the Daemon are disabled; the exit line shows, because the UI cannot prevent an exit.
9. A Decision Card for an Agent that has ended: the Card hides rather than answering with CONFLICT.
10. A `send` press while a previous send is pending: disabled until it settles, so no duplicate and no error.
Counterexample hunted: `⌥1`..`⌥9` jumping to an Agent whose `takeover.begin` answers CONFLICT (U107). The UI cannot know the Agent ended before the Daemon answers, so the error is allowed. The rule's `could have prevented` clause already covers this; no narrowing needed.
